applies_why: Yes; the judge text gives an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and states a ground for it, so K-S2 governs whether that ground is a single verse's non-statement.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: "a single verse does not state a link or its contrary" — I weighed whether it covers any absence of a live link to contradict (breach) or only a verse's own failure to state the link/contrary (not here).
why: The judge's stated ground is the defender's dropped curse limb leaving no live link, not that Jeremiah 22:30 as a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary.
